original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Bind the exact P112 tetrad-local masked decoder to the selected complex provider's 112 port labels, then price its rank-2 copy profile in a joint two-unpaid/rank-32 ideal budget.
scope_change_reason: The original task asks for a new child-rank shape with a full local invoice. This investigation instead resolves a missing source-binding step: the existing sharp P112 tetrad identity has an exact parity-graph isomorphism to the selected provider's actual ports. It tests the resulting copy profile against the current joint budget, but stops before claiming a physical supplier.
bottleneck_link: The selected result is limited by both suppliers. A source-bound full masked decoder at copy cost 112 fits the complex side's ideal two-unpaid/rank-32 budget above a=1/99, whereas the known rational decoder at cost 334 fails that screen. A dirty-input implementation and changed coverage interface are still required before this can affect selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after checking the full 112x112 port pairing, all 6,720 constrained masked entries, all 56 term ranks, and both exact moment controls. Do not expand into circuit construction until a physical dirty-input endpoint, two-unpaid coverage proof, rank-32 child implementation, restoration, hosting and consumer bill have an explicit allowance.
evidence: An explicit bijection maps the P112 root parity matrix to the selected complex provider's port Gram matrix on all 12,544 pairs. Transporting the 14 tetrad blocks gives a 56-term exact masked identity with copy profile {2:56}, total 112. With the inherited 192 phase units, 166 ideal rank-32 children, centre charge 112 and two unpaid coordinates, the complex moment at a=1/99 is 0.996649697627 and its ideal retained-conversion kappa cap is 0.0137876681081. The tracked bit-side two-unpaid/rank-32 relaxation caps at 0.0319843333739, so the joint ideal cap is 0.0137876681081. One-unpaid controls fail. No physical supplier or selected-kappa improvement is established.

open_questions.why_it_matters: This decides whether the 112-unit coefficient identity can replace the 334-unit rational decoder in an actual supplier rather than only in an ideal moment screen.
open_questions.first_step: Implement one mapped tetrad block (eight ports and four rank-2 terms) against the provider's actual local state interface; replay arbitrary dirty inputs and record every helper read and restoration operation.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current package binds coefficient labels only. It has no chronological source schedule, dirty-state circuit, owner map or physical invoice for the new terms.

open_questions.question: Can the complex and bit endpoints both justify two unpaid coordinates while retaining their rank-32 block profiles?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both one-unpaid controls exceed one at a=1/99; the ideal joint cap disappears if either changed coverage identity is not realized.
open_questions.first_step: Trace the exact data endpoint and unadvanced coordinates on each side, then verify a complete dirty-input instance before assigning the two-unpaid law to all calls.
